item.title: The landlocked rowers making waves at sea
item.description: Cornish Midland rowers train on Staunton Harold Reservoir in Derbyshire [BBC] Rowers from a landlocked club say it will be "amazing" to take part in the world championships for sea-going Cornish pilot gig boats. Midland Cornish rowing club is based at Staunton Harold reservoir in Derbyshire - which is only 10 miles from the point in Great Britain furthest from the sea - but competes against crews from places with long traditions of coastal rowing. The team row Cornish pilot gig boats, which are six-oared fixed-seat vessels, measuring 32ft (9.7m) and based on a design for a working craft dating back to the late 18th Century. Midland Cornish will be heading off to the world championshops in the Isles of Scilly, from 30 April to 2 May, which attract about 2,000 rowers. The Midland Cornish teams surprised some of the opposition at the Gig Racing County Championships in Plymouth representing Derbyshire [Supplied] Rower Katie Baines said their opposition was often taken aback to see a crew from the Midlands. "They're always quite shocked," she said. "They say 'oh, you're the furthest away from the sea you can possibly get'." The boats are still a familiar sight in harbours in the South West of England because, according to the Cornish Pilot Gig Association , there are over 90 clubs and more than 8,000 active gig rowers nationwide. But only one of those clubs trains on a reservoir more than 60 miles from the nearest stretch of open sea. Martin Pezzack was a star of Cornish traditional rowing in the mid-1990s [BBC] Midland Cornish was founded by Chris Baker, who moved from Cornwall to Derbyshire 35 years ago, but only got back into rowing in the past decade. Baker said his rowers were under no illusions about the challenge they faced. "I don't think we embarrass ourselves when we turn up," he said. "We try and coach the right way, so even if we're not at the front, we at least look tidy and that's half the battle. "It feels like quite an achievement to take a club from here and row against Cornish and Devon clubs that have been rowing for decades." Midland Cornish has around 30 regulars, while many clubs in the South West have hundreds of competitors to choose from. The Midland Cornish teams all share a love of being on the water [Supplied] However, what the Derbyshire team does have is a former multiple world champion as coach. Martin Pezzack, also from Cornwall, won his titles in the mid-to-late 1990s across a variety of traditional Cornish rowing disciplines. He said teaching people who rarely got to see the sea was even more rewarding. "It's strange," he said. "It's brought a new joy to it." "It's more of a sense of achievement this time because it's not just me - you're doing it with a bunch of people. "I'm helping people to develop and hopefully become champions in their own right." item.title: Manchester United boss Olid expecting tactical battle against Crystal Palace
item.description: Manchester United boss Olid expecting tactical battle against Crystal Palace Manchester United head coach Eva Olid says that she is expecting a tactical battle when her side come up against Crystal Palace this afternoon. The two sides meet at the Progress with Unity Stadium at Leigh Sports Village as they contest their latest Barclays Women’s Super League match. The game will see Manchester United head coach Olid go up against Crystal Palace boss Jo Potter for the first time since the pair met as head coaches of Hearts and Rangers in the SWPL. When speaking in the pre-match press conference, Olid said that she expects a tactical battle with Potter. “I expect a very competitive match,” Olid said. “They are having good games and their latest results have been good. It was such a competitive match when they played Tottenham on Wednesday and they won the game [on penalties]. “I know Jo Potter, we played each other in Scotland when she was at Rangers. She’s so competitive and her teams are always hard-working. I expect a really good match tactically and it’ll be intense.” Manchester United are unbeaten in 11 games in all competitions. While The Red Devils are in great form, Olid believes that opponents will be more motivated to end their run. She said “I think all of the teams are motivated when they face Manchester United. If they know that we are unbeaten in 11 games, I think it’ll add more motivation to the opposition. We just have to be focused and week-by-week try to win the next match.” After a tough start, Manchester United are now finding rhythm under Olid, but she believes that there’s lots to build on. She said “We are still in a process and we know that there are still a lot of things that we have to improve. “For me, it is so important that I see the team creating a lot of confidence with the ball and they start connecting with each other. That’s what we need and that’s the biggest step when we started the season to now; confidence with the ball and connections. “We still know that we need to keep improving and learning every day, but when you’re getting results, it’s better. We are in a process, but I think results are important at the same time.” Manchester United’s Barclays Women’s Super League fixture against Crystal Palace kicks-off at 12.45pm.

item.description: STEUBENVILLE – That Dover still had a chance in the fourth quarter of its rematch with Steubenville was equal parts shocking and unsurprising. Those who followed the Crimson Tornadoes in the regular season were well-schooled on their grit and resilience. It showed in Ohio Cardinal Conference wins against West Holmes and rival New Philadelphia, games it overcame deficits to win. But this was a three-score hole at Harding Stadium where second-half comebacks come about as often as winning Powerball tickets. Yet, here Dante Clark and Dover were, within a touchdown midway through the fourth quarter. Was another rally in store? Not this time. Dover rallied for a pair of scores and had the ball with a chance to tie with 4:04 left, but senior safety Braidyn Edwards intercepted a Dieter Weber deep ball over the middle — his second of the game — and Steubenville ran out the clock for a 21-14 win. It came on third-and-4, after two Steubenville penalties. As was often the case in this one, Big Red's big dogs made a timely play to fend the Tornadoes off. "Like I said at halftime, 'we've been here before.' We fought through those (West Holmes and Philly) games. This time the outcome wasn't in our favor." Dover finished a 9-3 campaign under second-year coach Matt Rees, who led the Tornadoes to a five-win improvement. item.title: The challenge that brought Nunes out of retirement
item.description: Amanda Nunes is one of four simultaneous two-division champions in UFC history [Getty Images] It was always going to take a special challenge to bring Amanda Nunes out of retirement. The Brazilian left the UFC in 2023 as the most successful women's mixed martial artist of all time, and with a strong claim to be the greatest ever, regardless of gender. A former featherweight and bantamweight champion, Nunes is the only woman to hold UFC titles in two weight classes simultaneously, and the only fighter, male or female, to successfully defend both belts. During Nunes' remarkable run, she beat some of the greatest names in MMA history, such as Ronda Rousey, Cris Cyborg and Valentina Shevchenko. After Nunes was eventually dethroned by Julianna Pena in one of the biggest upsets of all time, she then regained her title in emphatic fashion. Nunes was so dominant, she ran out of challengers and left the sport feeling like she had completed MMA. That was until Kayla Harrison came along. "When Kayla signed with the UFC and I saw the division with some new girls it excited me," said Nunes. "Because I cleaned both divisions and didn't have anything to do any more. That was when I was sure I wanted to do this again." American Harrison is a two-time Olympic gold medallist in judo who became a two-time PFL lightweight world champion after transitioning to MMA. After joining the UFC in 2024, Harrison won the bantamweight title in only her third fight with the promotion. The contest between 36-year-old Harrison and 38-year-old Nunes is being described by pundits as one of the biggest women's fights in UFC history. The pair are friends and former team-mates at American Top Team Gym, before Nunes left in 2022. They were originally set to fight in January, but the fight got postponed after Harrison required neck and spinal surgery. They will instead compete at UFC 334 at New York's Madison Square Garden on Saturday. Nunes beams with excitement at the prospect of returning to the octagon to fight Harrison, and she has lost none of her trademark confidence during her three years away from the sport. "I'm not here today as a challenger, I'm here today as a double champion," said Nunes. "I needed a break and did it at the right time for my mind, body and soul. "There's no hate. It's about the challenge Kayla brings and how great this will be for women's MMA. We want to prove who the best girl is in the cage." According to SPORT , Barcelona arranged for a representative to attend the international friendly in Buenos Aires to assess several players, with Martinez among the defenders attracting particular attention. The 28-year-old offers an experienced option for Hansi Flick, whose side continues to explore ways of strengthening their central defence despite the club’s financial restrictions. Notably, Barcelona’s interest is quite significant because Barcelona appear to be considering players who could contribute immediately rather than relying exclusively on younger prospects. However, any transfer of the Manchester United defender is complicated by his contract with the Premier League club. A perfect Barcelona fit? Martinez has established himself as an important figure in Manchester United’s defence since arriving from Ajax in 2022. item.title: The return of Ronaldinho: PR stunt or genuine comeback?
item.description: Ronaldinho return GFX - Getty/GOAL The 46-year-old retired more than a decade ago, but lower-league Italian side Ravenna insist that he'll return to action this weekend When Ravenna announced the signing of Ronaldinho in June of this year, the common consensus was that it was some sort of publicity stunt. Nobody truly believed that one of the most beloved footballers of all time was making a comeback at 46 years of age. Apparently, the return is real , though. Ronaldinho actually is going to resume his playing career with a third-tier team located on the east coast of Italy that's never even previously played in Serie A. Ravenna president Ignazio Cipriani said right from the start of this rather curious tale that the "dream" was for Ronaldinho to make his debut in the derby against local rivals Forli, and it's now set to be realised, with the 2005 Ballon d'Or winner expected to play some part in Sunday's Serie C clash at the Bruno Benelli. So, what on earth is going on? Why is Ronaldinho coming out of retirement? Is it just for one game? Or is he actually making a proper comeback?... 'Jogo bonito' incarnate Ronaldinho is revered as much for his smile as his sensational set of skills When Cipriani bought his hometown club in June 2024, his stated objective was "to make young people of Ravenna fall in love with football". What better way to do that, he thought, than to sign a player that he himself had grown up idolising? "I don't think there’s any other player who inspires such a love for the game as Ronaldinho does," the New York-based businessman told the Gazzetta dello Sport - and it's hard to disagree. One would be hard pressed to find anyone within the footballing community that doesn't like Ronaldinho. He's one of those very rare characters who is universally revered, adored all around the world because he is effectively 'jogo bonito' incarnate, a one-man carnival. There was one very obvious problem with Cipriani's plan, though: Ronaldinho retired in 2018 at 37 years of age, and hasn't played a game of professional football since parting company with Fluminense in 2015. However, the pair had developed "a genuine friendship" after being introduced by Lorenzo Tonetti, the former co-owner of the famous 'Giannino' restaurant that Ronaldinho frequented during his two-and-a-half-year spell with AC Milan between July 2008 and January 2011. Consequently, when Cipriani suggested a return to professional football with Ravenna, the World Cup winner "said yes immediately". "That’s just how things go with Ronnie," Cipriani told Il Resto del Carlino . "If there's a chance to have fun and excite people, he's all in." No mere marketing ploy Ronaldinho hasn't just joined Ravenna as a player - he's also come on board as a shareholder Ronaldinho's lust for life is well-known, and he was visibly touched by the hero's welcome he received when he made his first appearance in Ravenna at a lavish media event in August. item.title: LSU women’s basketball cruises past McNeese, Denver
item.description: After historic blowouts in the first week of the season, the #9 LSU women’s basketball team put up more standard blowouts in the second week of play. Monday, they trounced McNeese 100-43, and Friday, they crushed Denver 101-37. In total, LSU has outscored their opponents 461-137 in their first four games. Monday’s win over McNeese was most notable for the debut of Noa Morro, the 21-year-old freshman out of Spain. She played limited minutes, but she showed off her quick-release three ball and her ability to guard the perimeter. Combined with Anna Minaeva, she forms half of LSU’s post duo that they’ll need in their big games. LSU came out slowly with an 18-10 first quarter, but they found their groove with a 30-point second quarter. The Tigers cruised the rest of the way with solid play and got to 100 with a Mikaylah Williams accidental buzzer-beater three that she intended for after the buzzer. McNeese shot 9/44 from beyond the arc, something LSU had expected coming in. Jada Williams led the team with 12 rebounds, Mikaylah Williams led the scoring with 17 points and assists with eight, and MiLaysia Fulwiley had an absurd stat line of 13 points, seven rebounds, four assists, three steals and four blocks. Friday’s win over Denver saw LSU play more of their big lineup and get Noa Morrow more minutes than she was told she would get. It might also lead to the Tigers practicing their free throws a lot over the next couple days since they finished 19/32 from the line and 3/13 from the stripe in the first half. Other than that, it was a standard LSU blowout victory. The Tigers opened with a 20-12 first quarter before shutting the Pioneers down with a 22-2 second quarter in which they kept them from making a shot for over 12 consecutive minutes across parts of the first and second quarters. LSU ramped up the scoring with 30 in the third and 29 in the fourth, and Mikayla Williams sealed the hundo with a layup. MiLaysia Fulwiley led the team in scoring with 23 points while adding three steals and two blocks. Mikaylah Williams had 20 points, seven rebounds and a career-high six steals. Anna Minaeva led the boards with 10, and Jada Williams led assists with six. LSU is still in the midst of their long homestand next week. On Monday, the Tigers will take on Sun Belt preseason #1 Troy, and on Thursday, they’ll face reigning NEC regular season and tournament champions Fairleigh Dickinson, the latter of which I’ll be covering from the PMAC. Both games will tip at 7:00 p.m. and will be streamed on SECN+. Radio coverage will be on the LSU Sports mobile app or on Talk 107.3 FM in Baton Rouge.

item.title: REBELS: Edmundo - 'The Animal' who erased the line between genius and insanity
item.description: REBELS: Edmundo GFX - GOAL The forward was one of the most naturally gifted players Brazil has ever produced - but also one of its most troubled Sir Alex Ferguson told his Manchester United players before their 2000 Club World Cup clash with Vasco Da Gama that Romario and Edmundo's legs had gone. According to Mark Bosnich, it took them "about 20 seconds to realise that wasn't true". Vasco's famous front two ran rings around United's beleaguered back four - almost quite literally in the case of Edmundo, who, having teed up Romario for the game's opening goal by pouncing on a poor back-pass from Gary Neville, made it 3-0 just before the break with a strike so skilful that even Diego Maradona stated that only a handful of players in football history would have had the "imagination" to even conceive of it, let alone pull off. When Gerson played a short, diagonal pass into Edmundo on the edge of the area, a normal player would have laid the ball off to a team-mate. There was never anything normal about Edmundo, though. The man known as 'The Animal' stabbed the ball with his right foot, thus generating enough spin to flick it behind both himself and Mikael Silvestre, who had made the mistake of getting too close to the attacker. By the time Silvestre realised what Edmundo had done, it was already too late. The Brazilian was gone, taking full advantage of his still-explosive pace to win the footrace with Bosnich to the loose ball, which he subsequently dinked over the goalkeeper with his characteristic nonchalance. Tellingly, Bosnich wasn't even mad; he was impressed, describing it as "the most beautiful goal I've ever conceded", while Silvestre couldn't help but admire the way in which Edmundo had completely bamboozled him. "When you are not used to it, you do not expect such skills," the Frenchman told BBC Sport . "And only geniuses can do what Edmundo did to me for his goal." However, legendary American pianist Oscar Levant once said that he erased "the fine line between genius and insanity" - and, in the case of Edmundo, one could argue that it maybe never even existed in the first place. Beast of a player Edmundo was initially known solely for the quality of his play before his inner rage became a cause for concern There were reports of unusual, erratic or downright bad behaviour from the moment Edmundo began to make a name for himself as a prodigiously gifted teenager in the 1980s. item.title: Harry Kane: Man United have perfect opportunity to sign Englishman after Mauricio Pochettino arrival
item.description: Harry Kane: Man United have perfect opportunity to sign Englishman after Mauricio Pochettino arrival Manchester United’s pursuit of Harry Kane ended in a whimper after he signed a new deal with Bayern Munich last week. The English striker’s previous contract was due to expire at the end of this season, adding to speculation regarding his future and fuelling talks of a possible return to the Premier League. However, Kane has since poured cold water on those rumours by committing himself to the Bundesliga champions until 2029. That may have effectively ended all chances of a move to Old Trafford in January or even next summer. The English giants are in desperate need of a proven No. 9 in their squad, and Kane would have been perfect for the job. United’s striker woes United have been home to some legendary strikers in the past but have struggled to fill the position ever since Robin van Persie left. item.description: San Siro - The Scrum How do you get 80,018 people (yes, you read that right, EIGHTY THOUSAND AND EIGHTEEN) into San Siro during the international break? No Inter, no football, but still a ball, albeit an oval one for a change. On 14 November 2009, the All Blacks, New Zealand's legendary national rugby team, arrived at the Meazza to face Italy in a test match that made Italian sporting history. And what better stage than San Siro for an unforgettable Saturday? For the first time, the Meazza opened its doors for a rugby match that went far beyond sport. Italy was taking on New Zealand, the All Blacks, perhaps the most recognisable team in the world, even among those who don't follow rugby. It’s one of the most successful teams, with a remarkable 77% winning record. It was no ordinary Saturday in Milano. The city was filled with the familiar sea of black-clad New Zealand supporters, but above all with rugby fans from across Italy, eager to witness the day Italian rugby dreamed of making history. Kick-off was scheduled for 14:30 CET, making for a packed house not only at the stadium but also in Milano's bars from early in the morning. New Zealand fans had another important fixture to follow: at 8:00 CET, the All Whites, the national football team, were playing Bahrain for a place at the 2010 World Cup in South Africa after a goalless first leg. Mission accomplished, thanks to a header from Rory Fallon, a midfielder then playing for Plymouth in England's second tier. It was New Zealand's first World Cup qualification since 1982, sparking celebrations among supporters back home and in Milano. Just a few months later, New Zealand would face Italy in South Africa and secure a historic draw. It was exactly the kind of miraculous result Italy was hoping to achieve at San Siro. The Meazza erupts as the national anthem rings out, setting the stage for a special afternoon. The crowd can hardly believe its eyes when Italy takes a 3-0 lead through a perfectly struck penalty by Craig Gower. item.title: ‘I just lost it’: Isaiah Stewart says he still doesn’t believe what LeBron James said after he 'hit' him
item.description: Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images Isaiah Stewart and LeBron James were involved in one of the most viral on-court altercations in the history of the NBA. Back in 2021, when the Los Angeles Lakers faced the Detroit Pistons, James caught Stewart in the face while swinging his arm, leaving the latter bleeding. A sophomore at the time, Stewart was furious and involved in a huge altercation with James, which even resulted in a suspension for both players. Now, the former Pistons star has had his say on what happened. Isaiah Stewart says LeBron James hitting him was ‘personal’ For those unaware, in the third quarter of the game between the Lakers and the Pistons, James and Stewart got tangled up while fighting for a rebounding position during a free throw. As he tried to free himself, James’ left arm struck Stewart in the face, causing a cut right above his eye. To his credit, the then-Lakers superstar immediately apologised and even claimed later that the incident was ‘definitely accidental’. ( ESPN ) However, Stewart does not believe James to this day and feels that it was ‘personal’. He said on the Out The Mud Podcast : “Till this day I always say 100%, I know it was personal. You wind up, you hit me. He got a good hit. I’m bleeding. I definitely think it was personal. I’ve seen the interview of him saying it wasn’t. “He gave me a hit, and then I’m like, ‘hold up, hold up.’ And I got up, and then when I saw blood, that’s when I just blacked. I blacked, and I wanted to draw blood back. “Obviously, being a rookie, it’s a lot of stuff going through your mind when that’s happening. What you should do. How you should act. But man, once I saw that blood down my face, I just lost it. “I’m chasing him, trying to get to him around the court. And then I knew I wasn’t getting to him. So I said f*** it. I went to the back, ran to the back, they closed the doors. They said, ‘You got to clean these stitches up.’ I cleaned the stitches up. I got off the table, and I’m still trying to go over to their side. “And then my guy Troy Weaver said, ‘Look, you need to be the person we drafted.’ When he said that, it just clicked. And I said, ‘Let me stop it right here.’” Both players were ejected from the game, and on the following day, the NBA suspended them. James was given a one-game suspension for ‘recklessly hitting Stewart in the face and initiating an on-court altercation’, while Stewart was suspended for two games for ‘escalating an on-court altercation by repeatedly and aggressively pursuing [James] in an unsportsmanlike manner’. A lot has happened since, and the two players are in different stages of their careers – Stewart plays for the Memphis Grizzlies, while James plays for the Philadelphia 76ers. However, when the two sides meet in December, this will surely be the storyline heading into the game. item.title: Norway captain Martin Odegaard eyes revenge against Wales in crucial Nations League clash to keep quarter-final dream alive in Oslo
item.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-NOR-PRESSER - AFP Norway captain Martin Odegaard is targeting redemption against Wales on Saturday as the Scandinavian hosts fight to keep their slim Nations League quarter-final hopes alive. Sitting bottom of Group A4, Stale Solbakken's side must win in Oslo to avenge last month's defeat in Cardiff and remain in contention for the last eight. October setback leaves hosts bottom Odegaard is determined to settle the score after goals from Dan James and Neco Williams sealed a 2-1 victory for the Dragons at the Cardiff City Stadium in October . Despite reaching the World Cup quarter-finals this summer, the Scandinavians have suffered three defeats across their current Group A4 campaign. Those three consecutive losses match their total from their previous 23 outings combined, which featured 17 wins and three draws. Skipper demands improved home display Seeking to avoid losing four consecutive matches for the first time since October 2016, the Arsenal playmaker believes his team-mates are ready to bounce back in front of their own supporters . Reflecting on last month's defeat in South Wales, Odegaard said: "Our level was not where it should be. I think it's probably the only game for a long time where we haven't been playing to our standards. "Wales is a good team, a competitive team, lots of good players in big leagues and a physical team as well, and we were prepared for that. "But I think on the day we were just not showing up to our standards, and that's something we want to show [on Saturday], and we can do a lot better. We want to show a different version." Boss anticipates open tactical battle With Craig Bellamy's visitors also requiring three points to preserve their own quarter-final ambitions, head coach Solbakken expects an end-to-end contest: "It's like a boxing [match], going head-to-head, fist-to-fist. "I think Wales has always been a very attacking team under Bellamy. They've had great progress with the ball. "I think it suits the team with the offensive players they have, the speed on the wings and Harry Wilson back. And [Lewis] Koumas getting more minutes for Liverpool, so I think that suits them. "I'm not surprised that they will go all in, but it's our home game, so obviously I think they will also have their struggles with us. Let's see." Leaky defence faces attacking threat Tightening up at the back will be essential for Norway, as every one of their 12 matches since March's 0-0 draw with Switzerland has seen both teams score. That run represents their longest spell without a clean sheet since an 18-game streak between June 1980 and June 1982. Furthermore, conceding at least twice in five straight games is their worst defensive sequence since a six-match run in March 1976.

item.title: Ex-IOC chief Bach favours Russian participation at ice hockey Worlds
item.description: The former International Olympic Committee (IOC) president Thomas Bach speaks at the Stade de France during the closing ceremony of the Paris 2024 Olympic Games. Bach said he favours Russian participation in the Ice Hockey World Championships, which take place in Germany next year. (is associated with: «Ex-IOC chief Bach favours Russian participation at ice hockey Worlds») Michael Kappeler/dpa Former International Olympic Committee (IOC) president Thomas Bach has spoken out in favour of Russia's return to the ice hockey World Championship this May in Germany. "My opinion is clear and it has always been clear: it cannot depend on states, on governments, who can take part in sporting competitions, when, how, where and why," said Bach. Critics say Bach was close to Russian President Vladimir Putin when he led the IOC. Bach, 72, justified his view by saying that "autonomy and neutrality of sport" must be preserved. "Sporting qualifications count, not political attitudes," said Bach, who won a gold medal in fencing at the 1976 Olympics. Russian participation not favoured by all A fierce debate has erupted over a possible World Championship participation by Russia. The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled to readmit Russian ice hockey teams. That was followed by boycott threats for games against Russia from several countries, including defending world champions Finland. The German Ice Hockey Federation, which is hosting the May championships, does not want Russia to participate in the competition and is pushing for a swift solution from the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), the sport's world governing body. At the 2022 Winter Olympics in Beijing - just before Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine - the Russian ice hockey team reached the final but lost 1-2 to Finland.

item.description: Pascal Siakam and Indiana teammate Kelly Oubre Jr. celebrate a basket during the Pacers' NBA Cup win over the New York Knicks (Jeff Dean) The shorthanded Indiana Pacers held off New York 106-104 on Friday to leave the Knicks' bid for an NBA Cup repeat in tatters. The Knicks won last year's in-season tournament in what proved a curtain-raiser to their run to a first NBA championship since 1973. But after coming up short in their bid to erase a 14-point third-quarter deficit the Knicks fell to 0-2 in Cup play. They are not mathematically eliminated, but in three prior editions of the Cup no team with two group stage defeats has reached the knockout rounds. Pascal Siakam scored 19 points to lead a balanced Pacers attack. Aaron Nesmith scored 18 points, Kelly Oubre Jr. added 16 and Ivica Zubac and Andrew Nembhard chipped in 12 apiece to lead Indiana, who were again without injured star Tyrese Haliburton. Jalen Brunson scored 33 points and handed out 11 assists for the Knicks, who tied it at 87-87 early in the fourth quarter only for the Pacers to pull away again with a 15-2 scoring run. The Knicks made one last push, cutting the deficit to two, but Karl-Anthony Towns -- who scored 23 points and pulled down 15 rebounds -- missed a potential game-tying basket with nine-tenths of a second remaining. "Very proud of our team. We were pretty big underdogs coming into this game," said Pacers coach Rick Carlisle, whose team outscored the Knicks 50-30 in the paint. "Second half, it got difficult. New York is a championship team. They know how to make comebacks," Carlisle said. "Our guys stuck together and kept fighting together." item.title: 141 overs lost: Babar Azam, Mike Hesson suggest 'pink' solution for Pakistan's winter Test problem
item.description: Pakistan head coach Mike Hesson has called for the use of the pink ball in day Test matches at home to be seriously considered after rain and poor light disrupted the opening Test against Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi, which ended in a draw with nearly 141 overs lost. Hesson and Pakistan captain Babar Azam are open to the idea of using the pink ball in future home Test series, particularly during the winter months when weather conditions make it difficult to complete scheduled playing hours. The opening Test was repeatedly interrupted by bad light, forcing players to leave the field before the scheduled close of play on most days. The fourth day was called off during the afternoon session because of rain. Even before the rain arrived on the fourth day, umpires had to suspend play because the light had deteriorated to a level where continuing with the red ball under lights could have put players at risk of injury. The match was already heading towards a draw when play resumed on the fifth day. Pakistan were leading by just 45 runs with one wicket down as they looked to build a target for Sri Lanka. Pakistan ended up batting through the day before play was called off at 4:18 pm, almost two hours before the scheduled close at 6:10 pm. The decision came after Saud Shakeel was dismissed in the 90s for the second time in the match. The first three days had also seen significant interruptions, with only 14.2, 15.1 and 12 overs bowled in the evening sessions respectively. The International Cricket Council (ICC), following its last quarterly meeting, has approved the use of pink balls in day Tests as an option to address the problem of overs being lost due to bad light. Hesson believes Pakistan should consider the option for future home series. "It is certainly something that needs to be talked about for the future series," Hesson told the host broadcaster after the match. "It is going to be a challenge to play Test matches in this time of the year regardless of where in Pakistan. As the ICC have now allowed that to be an option, this is something that seriously needs to be considered before the series." Babar, however, pointed out that the short gap between the two Tests would not have given Pakistan enough time to prepare for a pink-ball match. With only three days between the two games, he said players needed more time to get used to the different conditions and behaviour of the pink ball. "You will need to prepare for it as we usually play with the red ball," he said in the post-match presentation. "A couple of days are not enough to prepare to play a Test with the pink ball. It is a good that we have it as an option, but the preparation for a pink ball Test demands more time."

item.title: Hermoso nears contract renewal until 2029
item.description: Hermoso nears contract renewal until 2029 Roma are keen to secure Mario Hermoso, who has become a key figure in Gian Piero Gasperini’s squad. The Spanish defender, who has made an excellent start to the season, has begun discussions with sporting director Tony D’Amico through his agent to reach an agreement on a contract extension, which currently expires in June 2027. As reported by Il Corriere della Sera , Hermoso’s entourage began discussions with D’Amico a few weeks ago to reach an agreement until 2029, possibly spreading the current €3.5 million gross per season. Negotiations are still in the early stages, but are set to continue, especially given the player’s central role in the Giallorossi’s coaching project. Hermoso’s situation has changed radically since the summer of 2025, when the Spaniard seemed destined to leave the capital after a disappointing first season and a loan spell at Bayer Leverkusen. The defender, however, decided to stay, gradually earning Gasperini’s trust and becoming a key player in the squad. The numbers confirm his importance: in his first 14 appearances of the season out of 15 games played for Roma, Hermoso has logged 1,049 minutes, second only to Wesley, who has 1,069. This performance has convinced the club to work towards extending their relationship with the 1995-born defender.

(Photo by Christian Charisius/picture alliance via Getty Images) In front of a largely empty Rajko Mitic Stadium in Belgrade, Germany came away with a 3-1 win over Serbia in their first of two UEFA Nations League matches during this month’s international break. item.title: Oklahoma-Ole Miss moved to Sunday due to Rebels' travel issues from nationwide ground stop
item.description: Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer (10) runs the ball for a first down against Mississippi during the first half of an NCAA college football game in Norman, Okla., Saturday, Oct. 25, 2025. (AP Photo/Alonzo Adams) (Alonzo Adams/AP) There won't be football Saturday in Norman, Okla. after all. This weekend's Oklahoma -Ole Miss matchup has been rescheduled from Saturday to Sunday after the No. 19 Rebels were unable to find a travel solution to arrive in Norman for Saturday's originally scheduled 3:15 p.m. kickoff. College football teams around the country ran into travel issues due to the nationwide ground stop that took place Friday . The Sooners and Rebels will kick off at noon on Sunday instead. "The Ole Miss football team was unable to depart Oxford Friday night due to the FAA ground stoppage," the SEC said in a statement . "After the stoppage was lifted, a late-night departure oculd not be accommodated by the charter company with which Ole Miss was contracted and the team's departure has been delayed until Saturday afternoon." Oklahoma made its displeasure with the situation publicly known. "As soon as we learned of Ole Miss' travel issues, we immediately began communicating with their staff and our conference leadership," Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny said in a statement . "We were told that Ole Miss explored every avenue to travel to Norman and play on Saturday as planned. But, unlike every other team traveling for competition tomorrow, they were unable to find a solution." The Sooners' frustration lies in the fact that several other teams were able to figure out Saturday morning travel plans. For example, Baylor-BYU was moved back from 2:30 p.m. to 6 p.m. when the Baylor was unable to depart Waco until Saturday morning. Making matters worse for Oklahoma, if it didn't agree to play Sunday, the SEC told the school forfeiture was on the table. "After multiple conversations with the league office, Commissioner Sankey informed us of his decision to move our game to Sunday, over our strong objection," Denny continued in his statement. "After continued discussions, he further informed us that our failure to play on Sunday at the directed time would result in a forfeit." The school said it will share game logistics and fan appreciation measures for Sunday's game at some point Saturday.
